correctness.rationale: For every positive repunit parameter, the fixed-point recurrences imply the alternating binary digit-sum identity. An exhaustive analysis of each possible incoming base-four carry establishes sharp finite-difference bounds and forces the boundary-letter constraints. Recurrence of all finite factors and reversal closure then produce exactly the two families of reduced Parikh vectors. A bounded-digit addition argument proves the global logarithmic upper bound. Literal finite checks at seven lengths corroborate but do not replace the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The new invariant was motivated by collapse of runs in factor complexity. Its exact spectra for a canonical automatic word at infinitely many natural base-four scales exhibit unbounded logarithmic growth, unlike the eventual periodicity of the published paperfolding reduced-Abelian profile. The result classifies every type, not just the total or finite cases, and identifies a digit-carry mechanism useful for further study.
